key_idea: The earliest crunch must be a front-wheel crunch, so the wheelbase is t_j - t_1 for some j: only O(n) candidates, each checkable greedily in O(n).
sketch: For each distinct positive d = t_j - t_1, scan the sorted times keeping a FIFO queue of expected back-wheel times: if the current time equals the queue head, match it as a back crunch; if the head is smaller, fail; otherwise treat it as a front crunch and push t+d. The queue stays sorted because fronts are processed in increasing order, so it is a plain array queue. Accept if the queue is empty at the end. O(n^2) = 1e8 simple steps. Pitfalls: d must be >= 1 (duplicates of t_1 give d=0), deduplicate candidates, and abort early when more backs are pending than elements remain. Verified against a multiset-matching brute force.
